Annotated Heatmap#

cl.annotated_heatmap draws a heatmap with annotation tracks along both axes. It returns one PlotSpec: the tracks are side bands that share the heatmap’s axes, so they zoom and pan with it (interactive=True).

The examples mark each gene with the cell type it is a marker of, stored as a variable column.

import cellestial as cl
from ggrust import *

data = cl.datasets.pbmc3k()
markers = {
    "Lymphocytes": ["CD3E", "IL7R", "NKG7", "GNLY"],
    "B Cells": ["CD79A", "CD79B", "MS4A1"],
    "Monocytes": ["LYZ", "CST3", "S100A9", "FCGR3A"],
    "Erythroid": ["HBB", "HBA1"],
}
keys = [gene for genes in markers.values() for gene in genes]
data.var["Marker of"] = "Other"
for cell_type, genes in markers.items():
    data.var.loc[genes, "Marker of"] = cell_type
data.var["Marker of"] = data.var["Marker of"].astype("category")

options = dict(
    keys=keys,
    group_by="cell_type_lvl1",
    variable_group_by="Marker of",
    column_annotations="Marker of",
    row_annotations=["cell_type_lvl1", "pct_counts_mt"],
    scale_axis=0,
)
cl.annotated_heatmap(data, **options)

variable_group_by draws group lines between blocks of keys, as group_by does for observations.

Track titles#

Each track has its own legend, so track titles are hidden by default. row_track_titles and column_track_titles name the tracks beside their band. annotation_legends=False keeps only the color bar.

cl.annotated_heatmap(
    data,
    **options,
    row_track_titles=True,
    column_track_titles=True,
    annotation_legends=False,
)

Key labels#

With many keys, key_labels labels only the ones given. Labels are spread evenly, with a leader line to each key, on the side opposite the column tracks. They are the key axis labels, so a theme styles them. An empty list labels no key.

cl.annotated_heatmap(
    data,
    **options,
    key_labels=["CD3E", "MS4A1", "LYZ", "HBB"],
    annotation_legends=False,
)

Group labels#

group_labels adds a bracket and text beside each variable_group_by block, for example its GO terms. Blocks without an entry get none. group_labels_width sets the text area relative to the heatmap.

cl.annotated_heatmap(
    data,
    **options,
    transpose=True,
    group_labels={"Lymphocytes": "T and NK", "B Cells": "B", "Monocytes": "Myeloid"},
    group_labels_width=0.3,
)

See Publication Figures for these options combined into a paper figure.
